connectors.lead: A connector lets your agent work inside a DCC app you already have. Installing one never changes the app itself, your scenes or your projects.
connectors.loadFailed: Could not read the connector list: {reason}
connectors.experimentalNote: not yet tested in the app itself
connectors.desc.unity: Projects, scenes, FBX import with PBR materials, builds
connectors.desc.godot: Scenes, nodes, scripts, import and export
connectors.desc.unreal: Levels, assets and import through Unreal's Python
connectors.desc.maya: Scenes, FBX and OBJ import with standardSurface PBR materials
connectors.desc.zbrush: Subtools, OBJ import, saving projects and tools; started from Meshy DCC Core
connectors.desc.freecad: Parametric modelling, mesh and CAD import including Meshy GLB, FEM
connectors.desc.material-maker: Procedural material graphs and PBR texture export
connectors.desc.houdini: Scenes, node networks, geometry, import and MaterialX materials
connectors.desc.substance3d_painter: Projects from meshes, PBR layers, baking and texture export
connectors.desc.openscad: Write and check models, export STL and 3MF, print bases for Meshy models
connectors.desc.c4d: Edits .c4d files in a project folder through c4dpy, without the app window
connectors.desc.roblox: Scene tree, instances and Meshy model import into a place
connectors.desc.3dsmax: Scenes and FBX import with Physical materials, Windows only

connectors.installing: Installing… this can take a few minutes.

skills.lead: Skills are the tools an agent uses inside a DCC app. The agent loads one when it needs it; loaded skills clear when the app restarts.
skills.instancesEmpty: Open a DCC app with its connector installed to see its skills here.
skills.instanceError: Could not read this instance's skills: {reason}
skills.noneLoaded: No skills loaded yet; the agent loads them when it needs them.
skills.mine.lead: Put a skill folder in one of these places and agents can use it in that app. The easiest way is to ask your agent to write it.
skills.mine.notFolder: Enter the full path of a folder that exists.
skills.mine.localOnly: Skill folders are on the computer that runs the gateway. Put skills there, then run:
skills.mine.pendingHint: Click “Reload in open apps”. A skill that stays in this state has an error; run meshy-dcc lint on its folder to see it.
skills.mine.addPlaceholder: Full path of another folder, such as skills on a team drive
skills.state.shadowed: Same name as a built-in skill; rename it
skills.write.hint: Send this prompt to your agent and replace the part in angle brackets with what you want.
skills.write.prompt: Use the meshy-dcc skill and its authoring guide to write a {app} DCC skill for me: <describe what it should do>. Put it in {folder}, check it with meshy-dcc lint, then reload and try it once.
skills.more.lead: From the Meshy marketplace. Installed skills load into the open apps.
agents.lead: Meshy DCC Core works with any agent that supports skills. Turn it on for the agents you use; the skill updates with Meshy DCC Core.
agents.foundEmpty: No agent was found on this computer. Pick yours below.
agents.foreign: Another meshy-dcc skill is already in this folder; it is left as it is.
agents.customHint: For an agent not listed, or a project's own skills folder:
agents.failed: Could not change the skill for {agent}: {reason}
agents.loadFailed: Could not read the agent list: {reason}

settings.remoteHelp: To use a gateway on another computer, register it on this computer and open the window again:
settings.dailyCheck: Check for updates once a day
settings.dailyCheckHint: You are asked before anything is downloaded.
settings.telemetryHint: Once a day: versions, connector types and tool-call counts. Never file paths, scene names or prompts.
settings.telemetryOffBy: Turned off on this computer by {reason}.
telemetry.notice: Meshy DCC Core sends anonymous, aggregate usage statistics once a day (versions, connector types, tool-call counts) to help improve it. It never sends file paths, scene or project names, or prompts. You can turn it off here or in Settings.
settings.devHint: Adds a collapsed Developer section to the sidebar: health, tool calls, traces, logs and the HTTP API. For troubleshooting and support.
report.title: Report a problem
report.lead: Tell us what went wrong. You see exactly what would be sent before anything leaves this computer.
report.label: What happened?
report.includes: Included: your description, versions and operating system, a diagnostic summary without paths or IDs, and recent Agent error reports. Nothing is sent until you click Send.
report.unknown: No answer came back ({reason}). The report may have been received, so do not send it again right away.
report.localOnly: Reports are sent from the computer the gateway runs on. Run this there to see what would be sent; add --yes to send it:
